_provenance.note: The finale card now holds nine bouts — backfill window B-2007 loaded them — so the tournament final is VERIFIED against our own ufc_bout_results row rather than merely sourced. The coaches' bout on the same card is still sourced only: B.J. Penn has no fighter row yet, so there is nothing to verify it against. Nothing is imported; the card's bouts live on the event page and are linked, not restated. House results, fight dates and classification are from the Nevada State Athletic Commission's Season 5 results record (tuf5-tuf6-nsac-reconciliation, reviewed by Justin Erickson). The draft's differing values are kept in each bout's corrections and superseded_result_sources; compatible method detail survives only where the commission category agrees. Printed readings: Matt Wiman vs Marlon Sims: the record prints "choke out ... rear naked choke"; read as Technical submission (rear naked choke) (approved reading).

_conflicts.detail: The source labels the opening bouts as an elimination round plus 'Round 2', 'Round 3' and 'Round 4' across episodes 1-7, which does not map cleanly onto a sixteen-fighter bracket. They are recorded together as the opening rounds in the order given, without being renamed into stages the source does not claim.

Our own records and the season source describe the same bout differently. Both agree on round 2 at twenty seconds and on Nate Diaz winning. The source calls it a TKO from a shoulder injury; UFC Stats records it as a submission. And the opponent is 'Manny Gamburyan' in the source and 'Manvel Gamburyan' in ufc_fighters — the same man under two spellings. Both readings are kept; neither is corrected into the other.

The season source calls him Manny Gamburyan; our fighter roster and ufcstats call him Manvel Gamburyan. One man, two spellings — the archive keeps the source’s and records the roster’s alongside it, so a lookup on either resolves. Found because the classification check reported the final as unverifiable when the bout was in our records all along.

Our result row records the final as a submission; the season source records a TKO on a shoulder injury. Both describe the same bout on the same card — Gamburyan’s shoulder dislocated and the fight ended there — so this is two descriptions of one finish, not two fights. Recorded rather than reconciled, because neither source is wrong about what happened.

_resolved_conflicts.detail: The source has Brandon Melendez beating Gray Maynard in the quarter-finals and then has Maynard losing to Nate Diaz in the semi-finals. Maynard cannot be eliminated in one round and appear in the next. Both bouts are recorded as the source gives them and the round is marked unverified, rather than dropping one to make the bracket tidy.
_resolved_conflicts.resolved_with: Nevada State Athletic Commission, Mixed Martial Arts Results — Season 5, The Ultimate Fighter — record nsac-2007-tuf5-09 (2007-02-21, "Quarter Finals") and nsac-2007-tuf5-14 (2007-02-28, "SEMI-FINAL BOUT")
_resolved_conflicts.resolution: Not two contradictory results: the draft inverted the winner. The commission records "Maynard won by tap out 4:07 of the 2nd round – guillotine choke", then Maynard in the semi-final against Nate Diaz ("Diaz won by tap out 1:20 of the 2nd round – Guillotine choke"). Winner corrected to Gray Maynard; method, round and time were already right.
